chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What is your view of the deceased when he dies, why is the twig placed with him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Punishment and Reckoning are staved off from him as long as the wood is wet.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And all the punishment is in one day, in one hour, the measure of what it takes to enter the grave and for the people to return. And the two fronds were made for that purpose, so no punishment or reckoning befalls him after they dry up, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.السَّعَفَتَانِ: The two fronds (of the date palm twig)

ai.seo_question: Why is a twig placed with the deceased in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the 'jarida' (twig) serves as a physical signifier for the duration of the initial phase of grave punishment, which is compressed into a single hour equivalent to the time of burial and return. This highlights the Shia scholarly understanding that while the soul undergoes immediate reckoning, the physical decay of the twig correlates with the mitigation or completion of this specific punitive interval, offering a tangible link between the material world and the barzakh state.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view of the deceased when he died and the twig was not made to be with him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Punishment and the Reckoning would be staved off from him as long as the branch is wet’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the Punishment, all of it, is in one day and one hour, a measurement of what it takes to enter the grave and the people returning, and rather, the two foliage’s have been made to be for that, thus there would neither be a Punishment nor a Reckoning after these two dry up, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, what happens if two fresh al-Jaridah (twig of palm tree) are not placed with a deceased?
He (the Imam) said, ‘Torture and accounting is kept away from him as long as the al-Jaridah (twig of palm tree) are fresh.

All tortures take place in one day in one hour for a duration within which people return and leave the gravesite. The two al-Jaridah (twig of palm tree) (branches) are placed for this reason, and after they dry there will be no torture and accounting by the will of Allah.’”
